children: Gabon's international bonds jumped on Tuesday after media reports said a government debt audit found the country's total debt burden was lower than previously thought.
The country's 2031 bond rallied 1.3 cents to bid at 87.475 cents on the dollar, Tradeweb data showed, while other maturities nearly matched those gains. (XS2113615228=TE)
Media reports showed that the results of the audit put the consolidated debt stock at 9,524.643 billion CFA francs ($17.01 billion).
Gabon launched an audit earlier this year to verify what the government owes. The country formally requested an IMF programme in March to help stabilise its finances.
